content.thinking:
The log shows the fraud scorer pod started on an A100 accelerator at onset, unlike the other two pods on V100, with no deployment change otherwise. rule_reading spiked from ~0.04-0.05 to ~0.15-0.19 right at onset while error_rate, latency percentiles, and request volume all stayed normal, pointing toward accelerator heterogeneity as the cause.

I can rule out bad-deployment (no deploys occurred) and autoscaling-pathology (cpu_limit_cores held stable at 3.0 throughout), with the rollout converged and no traffic split. Everything lines up with accelerator-heterogeneity as the root cause.

hypotheses.summary: A new pod (io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p) was placed on gpu-a100-0 (NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB) at the onset, while the other two serving replicas run on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards. No deployment landed and no config changed - the rollout is converged on a single revision and the change log is empty for the window - but the fraud-scorer model running on the new card answers differently, which is exactly what the paging rule (rule_reading, a fraud-hold quality measure) picked up: it steps from a ~0.04-0.05 baseline to ~0.15-0.19 right at 00:10:00Z and stays there, while error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency and request_volume all remain at baseline throughout. The log line 'fraud scorer serving on cuda device NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB' at 00:10:00Z pins the new accelerator to the same minute the rule departs.
